newsitem.title: FINLAND: POLL - Finnish 06 yield gap over Bunds seen falling.
newsitem.headline: POLL - Finnish 06 yield gap over Bunds seen falling.

text.p: The spread between the yield on the Finnish 2006 government benchmark bond and 2006 German Bunds is expected to fall to 28 bps by June from about 40 bps now, according to a Reuters poll.
A year from now the spread was expected to be tighter, at 20 bps.

The median forecast by 23 dealers, analysts and economists at banks and corporate treasury departments for the yield gap at the start of June was 30 bps in a 15-45 bps range. The mean was 28 basis points.
Nine respondents expected the yield spread to fall to 25 bps or less while two participants saw it at 40 bps or more.
Twelve months from now, the median forecast was 20 bps (mean 24 bps) in a minus five to 80 bps range.

Five market operators saw the spread at 10 bps or tighter. Of those, one bank anticipated a nil spread and another bank expected Finnish state paper to outperform Bunds with the spread at minus five bps.
Fourteen of the respondents forecast the spread at 20-40 bps. One market operator saw the yield gap at 80 bps after a year.
The poll was conducted on Thursday last week. Forecasts were collected on an anonymous basis.

Forecasts by Aktia Bank, Bank of America (London), Banque Indosuez (Stockholm), CD Derivatives Ltd., Davy Protos, Den Danske Bank (Copenhagen), Enso, Handelsbanken Markets Finland, Huhtamaki Finance, I.D.E.A. (London), Interbank, IVO, Kemira, Kesko, Merita Bank, Neste, Nokia, OKOBANK, Postipankki, SE-Banken (Helsinki), SOK, Unibank (Copenhagen) and UPM-Kymmene.
